status_summary: The science-related steps are partly in place, with the Mandate's IRIS elimination and default-model recommendations only partly matched. On 2025-01-20 Executive Order 14154 disbanded the interagency working group on the social cost of greenhouse gases and withdrew its estimates. In late January 2025 EPA's acting Administrator told members of the Science Advisory Board and the Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee that both panels were being reset. EPA opened public nominations on 2025-05-01; on 2026-03-09 Administrator Zeldin announced a reconstituted Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee (a chair and six members, serving 2026 through 2028, including two from state air agencies), and on 2026-04-17 a reconstituted Science Advisory Board (a chair and 36 members, 19 of them also serving on a subcommittee or the Clean Air committee). Executive Order 14303 (signed 2025-05-23) directs agencies to document uncertainty and use overly precautionary assumptions only where law requires or the action warrants them, and EPA's Deputy Administrator memo of 2026-04-27 implementing it moves hazard and dose-response judgments to regulatory program offices and adds a disclaimer to IRIS, but keeps existing and draft assessments public and does not end IRIS or mention linear no-threshold. EPA announced a reduction in force affecting its research office in July 2025, and the memo names the Office of Applied Science and Environmental Solutions as the lead for cross-agency risk assessment work. Legislation on the Science Advisory Board was not checked.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14154 abolishes the interagency working group on the social cost of greenhouse gases, withdraws its guidance and estimates, and directs the EPA Administrator to issue guidance within 60 days that may remove the measure from federal permitting and regulatory decisions (whether EPA issued that guidance was not verified).

EPA's acting Administrator tells members of the Science Advisory Board and the Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee by email that both panels are being reset; an EPA press officer says the move reverses politicization of the panels by the prior administration (date inferred from the weekday given in an NPR report dated 2025-01-29).

Executive Order 14303, Restoring Gold Standard Science, is signed (90 FR 22601, published 2025-05-29): agencies must document uncertainty, make influential scientific information and models public to the extent practicable, and use highly unlikely or overly precautionary assumptions only where required by law or pertinent to the action; the order does not mention dose-response defaults or advisory committees.
EPA announces a reduction in force affecting the Office of Research and Development, which had housed IRIS.
EPA renews the Science Advisory Board charter (date per EPA's release of 2026-04-17; the charter itself was not read).

EPA announces Administrator Zeldin's selection of members of a reconstituted Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee: a chair and six members for 2026 through 2028, two of them from state air pollution control agencies. The release says the charter was renewed on 2025-08-11 and nominations opened on 2025-05-01, and does not say which prior members were replaced.

EPA announces Administrator Zeldin's selection of a reconstituted Science Advisory Board: a chair and 36 members, 19 of whom also hold appointments to one of five subcommittees or the Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee. The release says nominations opened on 2025-05-01 and the charter was renewed on 2025-09-09, and does not say how prior members were replaced.

Deputy Administrator David Fotouhi issues a memo implementing Executive Order 14303: program offices make hazard and dose-response judgments (including uncertainty factors and dose-response curve shape), IRIS gets a disclaimer, past IRIS reliance is to be reviewed, existing and draft IRIS assessments stay public, and the Office of Applied Science and Environmental Solutions leads cross-agency work. The memo does not discontinue IRIS and does not mention linear no-threshold.

title: Overhaul EPA science: end IRIS, reset advisory boards, drop precautionary defaults
uncertainties: The two EPA announcements (2026-03-09 and 2026-04-17) were re-read in this review; they do not say which prior members were replaced, and the Clean Air committee release lists nominations opening on 2025-05-01, before its 2025-08-11 charter renewal. The 2026-04-27 memorandum was read in full; its subject line is truncated in the PDF text and it sets no deadlines. The January 2025 reset date rests on an NPR article that gives a weekday, not a date, and a number of removed members was not reported. EPA's own pages epa.gov/sab and epa.gov/casac block automated fetching, so membership rosters were not read. Federal Register notices show both bodies scheduling 2026 meetings (a Science Advisory Board meeting on 2026-10-19 and Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee meetings on nitrogen oxides). Not verified: whether EPA issued the social cost of carbon guidance required by Executive Order 14154, any EPA action on linear no-threshold or proprietary models, Science Adviser appointments, and the effect of the fiscal year 2027 request on IRIS (the Budget in Brief text read did not mention it). EPA's IRIS page metadata lists a review date later than its update date, unexplained. The IRIS web page is kept as a source, but its update date is a page check rather than an action and is not in the timeline.
